method.crossing: Same-floor interior segment intersection, sin(angle)>=0.2 and each segment parameter strictly between 0.01 and 0.99. Raw segment hits repeat people; uniqueGeometricPoints deduplicates (floor, round(x,5), round(y,5)); uniquePersonPairs deduplicates by ID.
method.stationary: Distance between a moving arrival/departure segment and another person's modeled assembly endpoint on the same floor <=0.03 figure units. Counts are geometric proximity, not body width, collision, or temporal coincidence.
method.scope: Within-cohort counts copied from source. Cross-cohort arrival checked for consecutive white groups 1->2 through 8->9 and additionally 1->3. Stationary checks cover 1->2, 2->3, 1->3; no timing inferred.
method.caution: B1 rest stand aisles and the single B1-to-B2 stair with three illustrative lanes are distinct physical resources. Same-lane reuse can be safe only when the earlier party and stationary queues have cleared. Floor designation and map scale remain unverified on site.

structuralFindings: full-diagonal-plan.py assigns stairLane by lie modulo three, but the allocator constrains distinct ordered feeder sources chiefly for blue columns; white feeder-to-stair lanes can cross at B1 entry.

White 2 uses STAIR as a stationary assembly node for 97 people in both layouts. The three lanes are tracks within one B1-to-B2 stair, not three additional independent stairways; capacity and hold location need field measurement.

Under the current source eligibility/assignment, white 8/9 use only 144M and 145 as feeder sections across both layouts. Requiring three distinct rest-section feeder outlets per three lanes there cannot be inferred from this model; redesign assembly/source constraints or retain a phased merge.
Counts from these geometric tests cannot certify crossing-free operational timing or physical body clearance.
